questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city as well as the courses offered at the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it overall pretty easy however I do believe there should be some more information regarding how and when to choose courses. It was newer really made clear when the deadline for this was.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a couple of e-mails of how to access the university's system and other than that I just had to to figure out myself how it worked.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very hard. Many companies will charge you huge fees for cleaning and administration, so my recommendation would be to either find something trough a private landlord or airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it can be very har to find something in a nice area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We basically were just provided a link to their website/system and had to choose courses which did not overlap in order to have a suitable schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. You could get any course you wanted as they did not have a limit of pupils.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To carefully read through the syllabus of each course.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was suitable. Some courses were a lot easier to participate in than others. Some courses were also very easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar apart from there not really being any reading/homework prior to each lesson.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ESN Network which is a society for Erasmus students hosted a lot of different activities so it was very easy to find activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To travel around Italy whilst you are there as the train tickets are cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To travel around Italy whilst you are there as the train tickets are cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their sense of time. The teachers were often a bit late and there was almost no classes starting in the morning - most classes started at 10 or later.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness, openness and way of socializing. The city and restaurants was always bursting with people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Not to worry about choosing the courses as you can change your courses throughout the entire semester and most teachers are very flexible. 

2) To find housing as early as possible as Milan is a city with lots of students and housing in the city centre is quickly unavailable or very expensive. 

3) To be patient with the teachers and the italian university system as they just do it in a different way than in Denmark but everything will be sorted in the end.
